channel.title: Pier & Point · Pier 70 Parcel H2
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Pier 70 Parcel H2 (Pier 70), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel H2: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2042 date comes from the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance. That was wrong. The Port's 2017 staff report (Item 9B, p.7) puts the Schedule of Performance in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) between the Port and the developer, which is a different agreement from the Development Agreement between the City and the developer. The report says the developer must complete phase 3 within approximately 25 years of project approval, but it never states the year 2042; 2042 is Pier & Point's own arithmetic (2017 plus 25 years). It stays labelled a legal outside date, not an expected completion.

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel H2: The 2026-09-29 entry for this record said the Brookfield construction halt could only be dated to 2022. That left out what Bisnow reports: its October 20, 2022 article says 'progress stalled in April', after 'a work stoppage earlier this year', so the halt is dated April 2022 (the year follows from 'earlier this year' in an October 2022 article). Bisnow is describing the 28-acre Pier 70 project's first phase as a whole, not this parcel in particular. The Real Deal's April 17, 2023 article says only that the developer halted construction 'last year'. The milestone stays marked approximate.

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel H2: Parcel H2 is now described as a flexible commercial-office/residential parcel (D4D Figure 2.1.1 stripes it both; the baseline scenario is residential) instead of commercial-office, and the map use is mixed; six stories is the commercial limit and nine the residential limit. The uncited Brookfield brochure claims (pure office, ~430,000 RSF for H1-H2) were removed; the 2042 completion date is the original 2017 outside date, now tolled by the down market delay (extended to December 26, 2026, Port Item 11A), with no parcel-specific date sourced; the claim that the block has no Assessor lot was replaced with what the sources show; the tree grove is described as running parallel to the Bay Trail; the Brookfield construction halt is dated 2022; the Aug 11, 2026 Port Commission minutes now back the informational hearing; and the Board of Supervisors vote on the Development Agreement shows first reading Oct 31 and final passage Nov 14, 2017.

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel H2: Port staff and Brookfield expect to bring proposed amendments to the DDA and related transaction documents (the proposals include extending the term of the DDA, Development Agreement and Master Lease by 5 years) before the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors 'by the end of this year or early next year'; the Port Commission minutes of Aug 11, 2026 say 'late 2026 or early 2027'. An expected date, shown at December 2026, the earlier end of that range (~2026)

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Parcel H2: Brookfield halts construction on the 28-Acre Site: The Real Deal (Apr 27, 2022, citing the San Francisco Business Times) reports 'Brookfield has halted construction' because of economic conditions, and Bisnow (Oct 20, 2022) reports that after the first phase's infrastructure and roadwork were completed 'progress stalled in April, with officials citing market conditions'. The Port's Aug 2026 report says the balance of Phase 1 horizontal work, largely the parks, is still to be built, so this was not the end of all Phase 1 horizontal work. The month is Bisnow's alone, and the sources describe the 28-acre project as a whole, not this parcel specifically (~2022)
item.description: Brookfield halts construction on the 28-Acre Site: The Real Deal (Apr 27, 2022, citing the San Francisco Business Times) reports 'Brookfield has halted construction' because of economic conditions, and Bisnow (Oct 20, 2022) reports that after the first phase's infrastructure and roadwork were completed 'progress stalled in April, with officials citing market conditions'. The Port's Aug 2026 report says the balance of Phase 1 horizontal work, largely the parks, is still to be built, so this was not the end of all Phase 1 horizontal work. The month is Bisnow's alone, and the sources describe the 28-acre project as a whole, not this parcel specifically (~2022). Source: The Real Deal (citing San Francisco Business Times), 2022-04-27; Bisnow (Joseph Gordon), 2022-10-20; The Real Deal (citing SF Business Times), 2023-04-17; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
